newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasoline steady amid refinery negotiations.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasoline steady amid refinery negotiations.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices were steady Monday, as prolonged maintenance and a possible strike between Unocal and its California refinery workers kept support to the market, traders said.
The union representing Unocal's refinery workers was in talks in Unocal Monday afternoon, ahead of a likely strike deadline of Monday evening, union officials said.
The four Unocal refineries affected can process 250,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude and make 20 percent of California's gasoline.
Ongoing maintenance at refineries run by Exxon, Mobil, and Unocal in Rodeo, Calif., also kept supplies tight, traders said.
Trade talk switched from March to April shipments Monday, with CARB gasoline in Los Angeles assessed 83/84 cents a gallon on Monday, even with Friday.
Deals for CARB unleaded were done at 83 cents in L.A., and at the same level in San Francisco.
